title: Anthropic won’t defend open weights. In June it made the same argument for itself.

content_html:
On Friday, 25 companies signed a letter defending open-weight AI. Three big names were missing.

By Monday, two of them had signed. That left Anthropic alone, and Silicon Valley noticed.

The pile-on

Nvidia, Meta and Microsoft signed “Open Weights and American AI Leadership” on Friday. Over the weekend OpenAI, Google and SpaceX added their names, Business Insider reported.

David Sacks, a venture capitalist and former AI adviser to the Trump administration, was blunt. “The entire tech industry (save for Anthropic) has come out in favor of open source AI,” he wrote on X.

“They won’t stop until they kneecap open source,” he added. “The rest of the industry needs to watch these guys like a hawk.”

Bill Gurley, a general partner at Benchmark, read it as commerce rather than principle. Anthropic’s reluctance, he posted, reflects that open weights compete “with their corporate economic strategy”.

Kai-Fu Lee, who founded the Chinese open-model startup 01.AI, put it more economically. “Who DIDN’T sign the Open Weight letter is far more interesting than who did,” he wrote, tagging Claude.

Anthropic did not respond to Business Insider’s request for comment.

What Anthropic believes, and has believed for years

Dario Amodei has argued consistently that developers lose control of a frontier model the moment its weights are published. You can withdraw a product. You cannot un-publish a file that thousands of people have already downloaded.

Anthropic’s alternative is gated access. Project Glasswing gives vetted organisations early use of its cyber models to find and fix security flaws, without handing over the weights.

That position has not moved. What moved is everyone else. OpenAI and Google were absent on Friday for the same reason Anthropic was, and they changed their minds over a weekend.

The argument Anthropic made six weeks ago

Here is the part missing from Monday’s criticism.

On 12 June, three days after Anthropic launched Fable 5 as its most powerful public model, the US government ordered the company to bar foreign nationals from Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Enforcing a nationality rule across a shared cloud service was impractical, so Anthropic switched both models off worldwide.

It was the first export-control measure aimed at specific AI models rather than at chips.

Anthropic called the order disproportionate. In its own statement the company said the capability behind the restriction was widely available from other models, and named OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 among them.

It warned that the precedent could “halt all new model deployments for all frontier model providers”.

Read that beside the open-weights letter. Restricting one category of capable model does not remove the capability. It removes it from the people who follow the rules. That was Anthropic’s case in June. It is the letter’s case in July.

The defenders who backed it

Anthropic was not arguing alone. Three days after the shutdown, roughly 100 cybersecurity leaders signed an open letter demanding the ban be reversed.

The signatories included Alex Stamos, formerly chief security officer at Facebook and Yahoo, along with Katie Moussouris of Luta Security, Rachel Tobac of SocialProof Security, Chris Wysopal of Veracode and Sophos chief executive Joe Levy.

Their letter said the action “has taken the best models away from defenders, created market uncertainty, and risked America’s AI leadership without any real risk to justify it”.

Change three words and that sentence describes what the open-weights camp says a ban on Chinese models would do.

The model that filled the gap

The sequel makes the timing worse.

Zhipu AI launched GLM-5.2 on 13 June, one day after Fable 5 went dark, and cited the ban directly as evidence that American models cannot be relied on. Its shares rose 33%.

Six weeks later, that same model did the forensic work on the Hugging Face breach after American closed tools refused to analyse the attacker’s code. It reviewed more than 17,000 actions.

That incident is the founding story of the Open Secure AI Alliance, which Nvidia launched on Monday with 37 members. Anthropic has not joined that either.

The distinction Anthropic could draw

There is a real answer available, and it is worth stating plainly because nobody in Monday’s pile-on stated it.

Anthropic wanted its model kept on sale. It did not ask to give the weights away. Selling access to a model you continue to control is not the same as publishing one that anyone can copy and modify forever.

Amodei has never claimed frontier models should be unrestricted. He has claimed they should stay in the hands of a small number of accountable labs, which is an argument against the open-weights letter and against the June order at the same time.

That is coherent. It is also, as Gurley noted, extremely convenient.

Why the silence costs something

Anthropic has one more reason to want Chinese open models restricted, and it is the least flattering one.

The White House has accused Moonshot of distilling Anthropic’s Fable model to build Kimi K3, the open-weight release that triggered this whole debate. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has floated sanctions in response.

Of every company in this argument, Anthropic is the one with a direct commercial injury to point at.

None of which makes the safety case wrong. It does explain why a company that spent June insisting restrictions punish defenders rather than adversaries has spent July saying nothing at all.

Anthropic has not drawn the distinction publicly. Until it does, the silence is making the argument for it.

content_html_zh:
周五，25 家公司签署了一封捍卫开放权重人工智能的信。 三个大人物失踪了。

到周一，其中两人已经签约。 这让 Anthropic 陷入孤立无援，硅谷也注意到了这一点。

堆积如山

Nvidia、Meta 和微软于周五签署了“开放权重和美国人工智能领导力”协议。 据《商业内幕》报道，上周末 OpenAI、谷歌和 SpaceX 加入了他们的名字。

风险投资家、特朗普政府前人工智能顾问戴维·萨克斯 (David Sacks) 直言不讳。 “整个科技行业（除了 Anthropic）都支持开源人工智能，”他在 X 上写道。

“他们不会停止，除非他们彻底削弱开源，”他补充道。 “行业的其他人需要像鹰一样密切关注这些人。”

Benchmark 的普通合伙人比尔·格利 (Bill Gurley) 将其解读为商业而非原则。 他表示，Anthropic 的不情愿反映出开放权重“与他们的企业经济战略”竞争。

中国开放式初创公司01.AI的创始人李开复的说法更为经济。 “谁没有在公开体重信上签名，比谁在公开信上签名更有趣，”他写道，并标记了克劳德。

Anthropic 没有回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。

人类相信什么，并且多年来一直相信什么

达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei) 始终认为，开发人员在权重发布后就失去了对前沿模型的控制。 您可以撤回产品。 您无法取消发布数千人已下载的文件。

Anthropic 的替代方案是门控访问。 Glasswing 项目让经过审查的组织能够尽早使用其网络模型来发现和修复安全缺陷，而无需交出权重。

那个位置没有动过。 感动的是其他人。 OpenAI 和 Google 周五缺席的原因与 Anthropic 相同，但他们在周末改变了主意。

Anthropic 六周前提出的论点

这是周一的批评中缺失的部分。

6 月 12 日，即 Anthropic 推出《神鬼寓言 5》作为其最强大的公共模式三天后，美国政府命令该公司禁止外国人观看《神鬼寓言 5》和《神话 5》。 在共享云服务中执行国籍规则是不切实际的，因此 Anthropic 在全球范围内关闭了这两种模式。

这是第一个针对特定人工智能模型而不是芯片的出口管制措施。

人择称这种秩序不成比例。 该公司在自己的声明中表示，该限制背后的功能可以在其他模型中广泛使用，并将 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.5 列为其中。

它警告说，这个先例可能会“停止所有前沿模型提供商的所有新模型部署”。

请阅读开放重量信件旁边的内容。 限制一类有能力的模型并不会删除该能力。 它从遵守规则的人身上消除了它。 这就是 Anthropic 六月份的案例。 这是七月份那封信的情况。

支持它的捍卫者

人类并不是一个人在争论。 关闭三天后，大约 100 名网络安全领导人签署了一封公开信，要求撤销禁令。

签署者包括 Facebook 和雅虎前首席安全官 Alex Stamos、Luta Security 的 Katie Moussouris、SocialProof Security 的 Rachel Tobac、Veracode 的 Chris Wysopal 和 Sophos 首席执行官 Joe Levy。

他们的信中表示，这一行动“剥夺了捍卫者的最佳模型，造成了市场不确定性，并危及美国人工智能领导地位，而没有任何真正的风险来证明其合理性”。

改变三个词，这句话描述了开放权重阵营所说的禁止中国模型会带来的后果。

填补空白的模型

续集让时机变得更糟。

6月13日，也就是《神鬼寓言5》下架的第二天，智浦AI就推出了GLM-5.2，并直接引用禁令作为美国模式不能依赖的证据。 其股价上涨33%。

六周后，在美国封闭工具拒绝分析攻击者的代码后，同一个模型对 Hugging Face 漏洞进行了取证工作。 它审查了 17,000 多项行动。

该事件是开放安全人工智能联盟的创始故事，Nvidia 于周一成立了该联盟，该联盟拥有 37 名成员。 Anthropic也没有加入其中。

人类可以得出的区别

有一个真正的答案，值得明确说明，因为周一的堆积如山中没有人说明这一点。

Anthropic 希望其模型继续销售。 它没有要求放弃权重。 出售对您继续控制的模型的访问权限与发布任何人都可以永久复制和修改的模型不同。

阿莫代从未声称前沿模型应该不受限制。 他声称它们应该留在少数负责任的实验室手中，这是反对公开权重信和同时反对六月命令的论点。

这是连贯的。 正如格利所说，它也非常方便。

为什么沉默要付出代价

Anthropic还有一个理由希望中国的开放模式受到限制，而且也是最不讨人喜欢的一个。

白宫指责 Moonshot 提炼了 Anthropic 的 Fable 模型来构建 Kimi K3，这款开放重量版本引发了整个争论。 作为回应，财政部长斯科特·贝森特提出了制裁措施。

在这场争论中的每家公司中，Anthropic 是唯一一家遭受直接商业损害的公司。

这些都不能说明安全案例是错误的。 这确实解释了为什么一家在六月坚持限制措施惩罚捍卫者而不是对手的公司在七月却什么也没说。

Anthropic 尚未公开做出区分。 在此之前，沉默正在为它辩护。
